escrow_required: no (the contractor may provide substitute security instead, and keeps the interest)
milestone_reduction: at 50% complete, one-half of the amount retained is released and later retention is capped at five per cent
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 32-1182, the prompt-payment section for owners and contractors, which lets the owner withhold "a reasonable amount for retention" and sets no percentage; § 41-2576 governs retention by the state
public_cap_pct: 10%; 5% after the contract is 50% complete; no retention at all for job-order-contracting contracts
release_deadline: within sixty days after final completion and acceptance
source_quote: A. Ten per cent of all construction contract payments shall be retained by this state as insurance of proper performance of the contract or, at the option of the contractor, a substitute security may be provided by the contractor in an authorized form pursuant to rules adopted by the director.
statutory_citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 41-2576 (retention by the state); § 32-1182 (progress payments by an owner, read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: not addressed in this statute
milestone_reduction: after 95% of the work has been completed, the department may reduce the funds withheld to an amount not less than 125 percent of the estimated value of the work yet to be completed
private_cap_pct: 5% of each payment, and no more than 5% of the contract price in total, on a private work of improvement under a contract entered into on or after January 1, 2026; not on a residential project that is not mixed-use and does not exceed four stories (Cal. Civ. Code § 8811)
release_deadline: upon final completion and acceptance of the project (state public works contracts, Cal. Pub. Cont. Code § 10261)
source_quote: The department shall withhold not more than 5 percent of the contract price until final completion and acceptance of the project. However, at any time after 95 percent of the work has been completed, the department may reduce the funds withheld to an amount not less than 125 percent of the estimated value of the work yet to be completed
statutory_citation: Cal. Pub. Cont. Code § 10261 (state public works contracts); Cal. Civ. Code § 8811 (private works of improvement)

escrow_required: not addressed in C.R.S. § 38-46-103
milestone_reduction: none
release_deadline: not specified in this section
source_quote: A property owner, contractor, or subcontractor shall not withhold as retainage more than five percent of the price of the work completed under the contract or subcontract.

escrow_required: yes on private work — an escrow account shall be established for all retainage, in a state or national bank or a savings and loan domiciled in this state; § 42-158q keeps that duty off any public building or public work of the state or a municipality, so none on public work
milestone_reduction: on a state agency contract the seven and one-half per cent drops to five per cent when fifty per cent of the contract is completed; none for private work
private_cap_pct: five per cent of the estimated amount of a progress payment for the life of the construction project
public_cap_pct: 7.5% on a state agency contract, reduced to five per cent when fifty per cent of the contract is completed; 2.5% on a Department of Transportation contract; 5% where the awarding authority is a municipality
release_deadline: not later than thirty days after the issuance of a certificate of final completion by the owner or the owner's authorized representative, or thirty days after the owner's equivalent written acceptance of the work (private work); § 49-41b sets no final-release deadline for public work
source_quote: No construction contract may provide for any retainage in an amount that exceeds five per cent of the estimated amount of a progress payment for the life of the construction project.
statutory_citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 42-158i, 42-158k, 42-158p and 42-158q (private work); § 49-41b (public work)

escrow_required: not addressed in Fla. Stat. § 255.078
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Fla. Stat. § 715.12, the Construction Contract Prompt Payment Law, under which an owner and a contractor "may agree to a provision that allows the owner to withhold a portion of each progress payment"; § 255.078 caps public construction only
release_deadline: same time limits for payment of a payment request apply regardless of whether the payment request is for, or includes, retainage
source_quote: a public entity may withhold from each progress payment made to the contractor an amount not exceeding 5 percent of the payment as retainage.
statutory_citation: Fla. Stat. § 255.078 (public construction); Fla. Stat. § 715.12 (Construction Contract Prompt Payment Law, read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: not addressed in Ga. Code Ann. § 13-10-80
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Ga. Code Ann. § 13-10-80, which governs public works construction contracts only; this record read no private-work statute
release_deadline: within 30 days after invoice at substantial completion
source_quote: Retainage to a maximum of 5 percent of each progress payment. At the discretion of the owner and with the approval of the contractor, the retainage of each subcontractor may be released separately as the subcontractor completes his or her work.
statutory_citation: Ga. Code Ann. § 13-10-80 (public works construction contracts)

escrow_required: not addressed in 815 ILCS 603/20
milestone_reduction: at 50% completion, retainage reduced to no more than 5%
private_cap_pct: 10% before 50% complete; 5% after 50% complete
release_deadline: not specified in this section
source_quote: A construction contract may provide for the withholding of retainage of up to 10% of any payment made prior to the completion of 50% of the contract. When a contract is 50% complete, retainage withheld shall be reduced so that no more than 5% is held. After the contract is 50% complete, no more than 5% of the amount of any subsequent payments made under the contract may be held as retainage.

escrow_required: yes
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Ind. Code § 5-16-5.5-3, which governs a state agency's contracts for a public building, work or improvement only; this record read no private-work statute
public_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Ind. Code § 5-16-5.5-3, which governs a state agency's contract for a public building, work or improvement, applies to contracts that "contain provision for retainage" and sets no percentage; whatever is retained must be placed in an escrow account
release_deadline: per contract terms
source_quote: provision for retainage shall include in their respective contracts a provision that at the time any retainage is withheld, the state agency and/or contractor shall place such retainage in an escrow account, with a bank, savings and loan institution, or the State of Indiana or an instrumentality thereof, as escrow agent selected by mutual agreement
statutory_citation: Ind. Code § 5-16-5.5-3 (a state agency's public works contracts)

escrow_required: not addressed in Iowa Code § 573.12 or § 573.14, neither of which says how retained funds are to be held; § 573.12(3)(b) is the nearest provision and is about who gets the interest they earn, not about an escrow account
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Iowa Code § 573.12, which governs contracts for public improvements only; this record read no private-work statute
public_cap_pct: 3% of each monthly payment (Iowa Code § 573.12(1)(a), as amended by 2025 Acts, ch. 29, § 1); § 573.12(1)(b) caps what a contractor may retain from each payment to a subcontractor at the lesser of three percent or the amount the subcontract specifies
release_deadline: 30 days after the completion and final acceptance of the improvement, when the unpaid fund is released and paid to the contractor, less a sum equal to double the total amount of any claims on file at the end of that period (Iowa Code § 573.14(1))
source_quote: The public corporation shall retain from each monthly payment not more than three percent of that amount that is determined to be due according to the estimate of the architect or engineer.
statutory_citation: Iowa Code § 573.12 (payments and retention from payments on public improvement contracts), as amended by 2025 Acts, ch. 29, § 1; § 573.14 (retention of unpaid funds, and when they are released)

escrow_required: not addressed in KRS 371.410
milestone_reduction: retainage held after fifty-one percent (51%) of the construction project has been completed shall not be more than five percent (5%)
private_cap_pct: 10% until 50% complete, then 5%
release_deadline: 30 days after substantial completion
source_quote: until fifty percent (50%) of the construction project has been completed in accordance with the contract, a contracting entity, contractor, or subcontractor may withhold no more than ten percent (10%) retainage from the amount of any undisputed payment due, and retainage held after fifty-one percent (51%) of the construction project has been completed shall not be more than five percent (5%) of the total contract amount.

escrow_required: yes on private work — under R.S. 9:4857 retainage withheld on a private contract of fifty thousand dollars or more shall be deposited into an interest bearing escrow account, and the Section does not reach a single or double family residence or the listed industrial facilities; none on public work, where R.S. 38:2249 instead lets the contractor withdraw the retained amount by depositing security of equal value
milestone_reduction: none in this Section; the cap turns on the size of the project rather than on a completion milestone
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap; the Private Works Act governs how private retainage is escrowed and bonded rather than how much may be withheld, and R.S. 9:4858 leaves the amount to the contract
public_cap_pct: ten percent of the contract price on projects of less than five hundred thousand dollars, and five percent of the contract price on projects of five hundred thousand dollars or more
release_deadline: on public work, until the expiration of forty-five days after the recordation of formal acceptance of such work, or notice of default by the contractor or subcontractor
source_quote: A. No contracts for the construction, alteration, or repair of any public works executed in conformity with this Part shall provide that the state or any of its agencies, boards, or subdivisions or any other public entity letting such a contract may withhold payment of more than ten percent of the contract price on projects of less than five hundred thousand dollars, and five percent of the contract price on projects of five hundred thousand dollars or more until the expiration of forty-five days after the recordation of formal acceptance of such work, or notice of default by the contractor or subcontractor.
statutory_citation: La. Rev. Stat. §§ 38:2248 and 38:2249 on public works, and §§ 9:4857 and 9:4858 of the Private Works Act on private works; the public Section may not be waived and does not apply to the Department of Transportation and Development

escrow_required: optional (public retainage may be deposited in an interest-bearing escrow account, and interest is then paid pro rata)
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: 5% of the contract price, where the contractor has furnished 100% performance and payment security; the section does not apply to a contract under $100,000
public_cap_pct: 5% of the total amount, where the contractor has furnished 100% payment security and 100% performance security (State procurement contracts)
release_deadline: within 90 days after the date of substantial completion
source_quote: (e) Undisputed retention proceeds retained by an owner under this section shall be paid within 90 days after the date of substantial completion, as defined by the applicable contract or subcontract.
statutory_citation: Md. Code, Real Prop. § 9-304; Md. Code, State Fin. & Proc. § 13-225

escrow_required: not addressed in Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 149, § 29F; Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 30, § 39K
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: 5% of any progress payment, on a contract for construction with an original contract price of not less than $3,000,000, excluding projects of 1 to 4 dwelling units
public_cap_pct: 5% of the approved amount of each periodic payment on public building contracts
release_deadline: not later than 30 days following submission of the application
source_quote: (b) No contract for construction shall include retainage that exceeds 5 per cent of any progress payment.
statutory_citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 149, § 29F; Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 30, § 39K

escrow_required: public only (deposited in an interest bearing account in a regulated financial institution in this state, unless the retained funds are to come from a state or federal grant and have not yet been paid to the public agency)
milestone_reduction: After the work is 50% in place, additional retainage shall not be withheld unless the public agency determines that the contractor is not making satisfactory progress
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap; Act 524 of 1980 reaches only a facility that is paid for with public funds or a special assessment
public_cap_pct: Not more than 10% of the dollar value of all work in place until work is 50% in place
release_deadline: released to a contractor together with the final progress payment, which § 125.1562(3) times at thirty days after the architect or professional engineer certifies the work is in place, or fifteen days after the public agency receives the state or federal funds, whichever is later
source_quote: (1) To assure proper performance of a construction contract by the contractor, a public agency may retain a portion of each progress payment otherwise due as provided in this section.
statutory_citation: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 125.1561 to 125.1563 (Act 524 of 1980); § 125.1561(c) puts a contract worth less than $30,000.00, or one providing for 3 or fewer payments, outside "construction contract", and § 125.1561(h) puts the state transportation department, a school district, a junior or community college, the Michigan state housing development authority and a municipal electric utility outside "public agency"

escrow_required: not addressed in Minn. Stat. § 337.10
milestone_reduction: owner may reduce or eliminate retainage if work is progressing satisfactorily
release_deadline: 60 days after substantial completion
source_quote: Retainage on a building and construction contract may not exceed five percent. An owner or owner's agent may reduce the amount of retainage and may eliminate retainage on any monthly contract payment if, in the owner's opinion, the work is progressing satisfactorily.
statutory_citation: Minn. Stat. § 337.10

escrow_required: not addressed in RSMo § 34.057
milestone_reduction: public owner may reduce or eliminate retainage if work is proceeding satisfactorily
private_cap_pct: 10% of each payment due from the owner to the contractor, on private construction projects other than single-family residential construction and other residential construction of four or fewer units; the contract may let the owner retain more if the contractor's performance is not in accordance with the contract (RSMo §§ 436.303 and 436.336)
release_deadline: 30 days after acceptance and receipt of required documentation (public works, RSMo § 34.057)
source_quote: Retainage withheld on any construction contract or subcontract for public works projects shall not exceed five percent of the value of the contract or subcontract.
statutory_citation: RSMo § 34.057 (public works); RSMo §§ 436.303 and 436.336 (private construction work)

escrow_required: not addressed in Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 45-1202, 45-1203, 45-1204
milestone_reduction: at 50% complete, no more than five percent of any additional progress payment, conditional on assurances of continued performance and financial responsibility
private_cap_pct: 10%, and no more than 5% of additional progress payments once the withheld scope is 50% complete
public_cap_pct: 10% for a political subdivision; the Construction Prompt Pay Act does not reach State of Nebraska contracts
release_deadline: within forty-five days after the project, or a designated portion thereof, is substantially complete
source_quote: (1) For retainage, in an amount not to exceed the amount specified in the applicable contract, which shall not exceed a rate of ten percent. If the scope of work for the contractor or subcontractor from which retainage is withheld is fifty percent complete and if the contractor or subcontractor has performed work in accordance with the provisions in the applicable contract, no more than five percent of any additional progress payment may be withheld as retainage if the contractor or subcontractor provides or has provided satisfactory and reasonable assurances of continued performance and financial responsibility to complete the work;

escrow_required: not addressed in NRS 338.515
milestone_reduction: after 50% of the work has been completed, the public body may pay remaining progress payments without withholding additional retainage
private_cap_pct: 5% of each payment to the prime contractor, where the agreement authorizes the owner to withhold a retention amount; NRS 624.609 does not apply to an agreement with a natural person who owns a single-family residence or to a public work (NRS 624.622)
release_deadline: within 30 days after occupancy, use, or recording of notice of completion, whichever occurs first (public works, NRS 338.515)
source_quote: Ninety-five percent of the amount of any progress payment must be paid and 5 percent withheld as retainage until 50 percent of the work required by the contract has been performed.
statutory_citation: NRS 338.515 (public works); NRS 624.609 and 624.622 (private works of improvement)

escrow_required: no — the act prohibits withholding outright rather than regulating how retainage is held
milestone_reduction: none — withholding is prohibited from the first progress payment
private_cap_pct: 0% — the same prohibition binds a private owner, but the Prompt Payment Act does not apply to construction contracts for residential property containing four or fewer dwelling units
public_cap_pct: 0% — the act repeals the retainage provisions of Chapter 57, Article 28 and prohibits the withholding of amounts due for work performed
release_deadline: no retainage may be withheld, so there is nothing to release; an undisputed request for payment must be paid within twenty-one days after the owner receives it
source_quote: RELATING TO TRADE PRACTICES; CHANGING THE NAME OF THE RETAINAGE ACT TO THE PROMPT PAYMENT ACT; ELIMINATING PROVISIONS OF CHAPTER 57, ARTICLE 28 NMSA 1978 CONCERNING RETAINAGE; PROHIBITING THE WITHHOLDING OF AMOUNTS DUE FOR WORK PERFORMED; AMENDING AND REPEALING SECTIONS OF THE NMSA 1978.
statutory_citation: NMSA 1978 §§ 57-28-1 to 57-28-11 (Prompt Payment Act), as amended by Laws 2007, ch. 213 (S.B. 604, 2007 Regular Session); § 57-28-2 puts the department of transportation outside the act’s definition of "owner"

escrow_required: not addressed in N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 756-c or Gen. Mun. Law § 106-b
milestone_reduction: none
public_cap_pct: 5% of each progress payment; up to 10% where the public owner does not require both a performance bond and a labor and material bond in the full amount of the contract
release_deadline: 30 days after final approval of the work (private contracts, Gen. Bus. Law § 756-c)
source_quote: By mutual agreement of the relevant parties an owner may retain no more than five per centum of the contract sum as retainage. A contractor or subcontractor may also retain no more than five per centum for retainage and in no case shall retainage exceed the actual percentage retained by the owner. Retainage shall be released by the owner to the contractor no later than thirty days after the final approval of the work under a construction contract.
statutory_citation: N.Y. Gen. Mun. Law § 106-b (public work); N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 756-c (private contracts)

escrow_required: not addressed in N.C. Gen. Stat. § 143-134.1
milestone_reduction: retainage eliminated after 50% complete with surety consent
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 22C (Payments to Subcontractors), which sets no percentage for an owner and limits what a contractor may withhold from a subcontractor to "a reasonable amount for retainage not to exceed the initial percentage retained by the owner" (§ 22C-4); § 143-134.1 governs public construction contracts only
release_deadline: 60 days after substantial completion or beneficial occupancy
source_quote: The owner shall not retain more than five percent (5%) of any periodic payment due a prime contractor.
statutory_citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 143-134.1 (public construction contracts); N.C. Gen. Stat. § 22C-4 (payments to subcontractors, read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: optional, public work only — money due is paid to the contractor or deposited in an escrow account selected by mutual agreement between the contractor and the public owner
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Ohio Rev. Code § 4113.61, the prompt-payment section, under which a contractor may reduce a subcontractor's payment "by any retainage provision contained in the contract"; §§ 153.12 and 153.13 govern public improvements only
release_deadline: within thirty days of substantial completion, occupation, use or acceptance of the project; any amount still withheld pending final completion, not later than thirty days after final completion
source_quote: Partial payments to the contractor for labor performed under either a unit or lump sum price contract shall be made at a rate of not less than ninety-six per cent of the estimates prepared by the contractor and approved by the architect or engineer.
statutory_citation: Ohio Rev. Code §§ 153.12, 153.13 and 153.63 (public improvements); § 4113.61 (prompt payment, read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: yes (contracts exceeding $500,000)
milestone_reduction: none
release_deadline: interest commences 30 days after completion and acceptance
source_quote: An owner, contractor or subcontractor may withhold as retainage an amount equal to not more than five percent of the contract price of the work completed.

escrow_required: not addressed in 73 P.S. § 509 (Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act, Section 9)
milestone_reduction: contractor or subcontractor may post a maintenance bond for 120% of retainage upon reaching substantial completion to facilitate release (private work, 73 P.S. § 509)
private_cap_pct: no statutory percentage cap in the Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act (73 P.S. § 509), which sets when retainage must be released and no percentage; a contractor may withhold retainage from a subcontractor "in accordance with their agreement"
public_cap_pct: 10% of the amount due the contractor until 50% of the contract is completed, then no more than 5% after that, of the value of completed work based on monthly progress payment requests (62 Pa.C.S. § 3921(a)); a lower limit applies where the Department of General Services is the government agency (§ 3921(b))
release_deadline: 30 days after final acceptance of the work (private work, 73 P.S. § 509, the Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act)
source_quote: If payments under a construction contract are subject to retainage, any amounts which have been retained during the performance of the contract and which are due to be released to the contractor upon final completion shall be paid within 30 days after final acceptance of the work.
statutory_citation: 73 P.S. § 509 (Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act, Section 9 — private work); 62 Pa.C.S. § 3921 (retainage on a government agency's public works contract)

escrow_required: not addressed in S.C. Code Ann. § 29-6-40
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in S.C. Code Ann. Title 29, Chapter 6, where § 29-6-40 lets an owner, contractor or subcontractor withhold "a reasonable amount for retainage" and sets no percentage
public_cap_pct: 3.5% of each progress payment or installment on a contract or subcontract for construction with the State or a general contractor (S.C. Code Ann. § 11-35-3030(4)(a)); Title 29, Chapter 6, whose prompt-payment rules reach a government owner too, sets no percentage
release_deadline: 21 days for owner to contractor; 7 days for contractor to subcontractor after receipt (S.C. Code Ann. § 29-6-30, in the prompt-payment chapter, whose "owner" includes a government agency)
source_quote: Nothing in this chapter prevents the owner, the contractor, or a subcontractor from withholding application and certification for payment because of the following: unsatisfactory job progress, defective construction not remedied, disputed work, third party claims filed or reasonable evidence that claim will be filed, failure of contractor or subcontractor to make timely payments for labor, equipment, and materials, damage to owner, contractor, or another subcontractor, reasonable evidence that contract or subcontract cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the contract or subcontract sum, or a reasonable amount for retainage.
statutory_citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 29-6-40 (prompt payment, whose "owner" includes any state, local, or municipal government agency); S.C. Code Ann. § 11-35-3030(4) (retention on state construction contracts)

escrow_required: yes
milestone_reduction: none
release_deadline: 90 days after completion of the work or 90 days after substantial completion
source_quote: (a) All construction contracts on any project in this state, both public and private, may provide for the withholding of retainage; provided, however, that the retainage amount may not exceed five percent (5%) of the amount of the contract.
statutory_citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-34-103

escrow_required: optional (contracts ≥$10M, by agreement)
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Tex. Prop. Code ch. 53, which treats retainage as "the amount specified to be retained in the contract" (§ 53.025) and separately requires the owner to reserve part of the contract price until 30 days after the work is completed (§ 53.101); Gov't Code § 2252.032 governs public works contracts only
release_deadline: upon completion of the work required to be performed under the contract
source_quote: if the total value of a public works contract is less than $5 million, a governmental entity may not withhold retainage in an amount that exceeds 10 percent of the contract price and the rate of retainage may not exceed 10 percent for any item in a bid schedule or schedule of values for the project, including materials and equipment delivered on site to be installed;
statutory_citation: Tex. Gov't Code § 2252.032 (public works contracts); Tex. Prop. Code §§ 53.025 and 53.101 (read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: not addressed in Va. Code § 2.2-4333
milestone_reduction: none
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Va. Code § 11-4.6, the payment section for construction contracts with an owner other than a public body, one subdivision of which says it does not "apply to or prohibit the inclusion of any retainage provisions in a construction contract"; § 2.2-4333 governs public contracts only
release_deadline: included in the final payment
source_quote: the contractor shall be paid at least ninety-five percent of the earned sum when payment is due, with no more than five percent being retained to ensure faithful performance of the contract. All amounts withheld may be included in the final payment.
statutory_citation: Va. Code § 2.2-4333 (public contracts); Va. Code § 11-4.6 (construction contracts with a private owner, read for the private-project field)

escrow_required: optional
milestone_reduction: contractor may request retainage be reduced to 100% of the value of work remaining
private_cap_pct: 5% of the contract price of the work completed, on private construction projects other than single-family residential construction of less than 12 units (RCW 60.30.010)
release_deadline: 60 days after completion of all contract work (public improvement contracts, RCW 60.28.011)
source_quote: public improvement contracts must provide, and public bodies must reserve, a contract retainage not to exceed five percent of the moneys earned by the contractor as a trust fund for the protection and payment of: (i) The claims of any person arising under the contract
statutory_citation: RCW 60.28.011 (public improvement contracts); RCW 60.30.010 (private construction projects)

escrow_required: not addressed in Wis. Stat. § 66.0901(9)(b)
milestone_reduction: at 50% completion, no further retainage withheld (full payments resume)
private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in Wis. Stat. § 66.0901(9)(b), which governs a municipality's contracts for a public work or building only; this record read no private-work statute
public_cap_pct: 5% until 50% complete; 0% after 50% complete (unless unsatisfactory progress)
release_deadline: not specified in this section — payment of an amount retained upon substantial completion is permissive, not a deadline
source_quote: The retainage shall be an amount equal to not more than 5 percent of the estimate until 50 percent of the work has been completed. At 50 percent completion, further partial payments shall be made in full to the contractor and no additional amounts may be retained unless the architect or engineer certifies that the job is not proceeding satisfactorily, but amounts previously retained shall not be paid to the contractor.
statutory_citation: Wis. Stat. § 66.0901(9)(b) (a municipality's public works contracts)
